Title: Retrosynthesis planning
Description: Attempts to plan a synthesis for a target molecule and reports whether a route was found, how many steps it needs, how many precursors it calls for and how many of those are purchasable. AiZynthFinder, from Genheden and colleagues at AstraZeneca, runs a Monte Carlo tree search guided by a neural network policy over reaction templates learned from US patent reactions, stopping once precursors appear in a ZINC building-block stock. The authors caution that the route score was built to steer the search rather than to judge route quality, and targets left unsolved return empty values.
Interpretation: Best route score approaching one when solved, with counts of reaction steps, precursors and purchasable precursors.
